app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43 — P1 confidence 100: `:website_name,` bypasses the `untrusted_attributes :website` restriction, so anonymous viewers still receive the hidden website host/path when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` suppresses the website field.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — [P1, confidence 100] `def include_website_name; website.present?; end` bypasses `scope.restrict_user_fields?`, exposing a restricted TL0 user's website hostname and same-site path to anonymous API clients even though `website` itself is hidden.

spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11 — [P1, confidence 100] `let(:untrusted_attributes) { %i{bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background} }` omits the new `website_name`, so the anonymous-TL0 regression spec stays green while the serializer exposes the otherwise-suppressed website host and path.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — (P2, confidence 100) The case-sensitive comparison `if website_host == discourse_host` misclassifies `https://EXAMPLE.COM/user` as an external domain when `Discourse.current_hostname` is `example.com`, so the serializer returns `EXAMPLE.COM` and omits the path despite DNS hostnames being case-insensitive.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the comparison `website_host == discourse_host` on line 141 is case-sensitive. Looking at the diff, `URI(website.to_s).host` returns the host as-is from the URL, and `Discourse.current_hostname` returns the configured hostname. If a user enters 'https://EXAMPLE.COM/user' and the discourse hostname is 'example.com', the comparison would fail despite DNS hostnames being case-insensitive per RFC standards. This would cause the code to fall through to other conditions and potentially return just 'EXAMPLE.COM' without the path, when it should include the path since it's the same domain. This is a real edge case bug in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43 — P1 confidence 100: `:website_name,` bypasses the `untrusted_attributes :website` restriction, so anonymous viewers still receive the hidden website host/path when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` suppresses the website field.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, `website` is listed under `untrusted_attributes` (line 43 shows it's in the attributes list, and the existing code structure shows `untrusted_attributes` method exists). The new `website_name` attribute is added to the regular attributes list (line 43: `:website_name,`) but is NOT added to the `untrusted_attributes` list. The `include_website_name` method only checks `website.present?` and does not check `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. This means when `website` is restricted for anonymous users via `untrusted_attributes`, the `website_name` (which derives from the website URL) would still be exposed, leaking the website host/path information that should be hidden.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — [P1, confidence 100] `def include_website_name; website.present?; end` bypasses `scope.restrict_user_fields?`, exposing a restricted TL0 user's website hostname and same-site path to anonymous API clients even though `website` itself is hidden.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security issue. Looking at the diff, the `website` method has an `include_website?` check that respects `scope.restrict_user_fields?` (visible in the existing code pattern). However, the new `include_website_name?` method only checks `website.present?` without any restriction check. This means `website_name` could be exposed even when `website` itself is hidden due to trust level restrictions. The serializer shows `website` is in `untrusted_attributes` (line 43), meaning it should be restricted for TL0 users, but `website_name` doesn't follow the same restriction pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11 — [P1, confidence 100] `let(:untrusted_attributes) { %i{bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background} }` omits the new `website_name`, so the anonymous-TL0 regression spec stays green while the serializer exposes the otherwise-suppressed website host and path.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security issue. Looking at the diff, the serializer adds `website_name` as a new attribute (line 43 in user_serializer.rb). The `untrusted_attributes` method (referenced in the finding at spec line 11, though not shown in the diff) controls which attributes are hidden for anonymous/low-trust users. Since `website_name` is derived from `website` (which is already in untrusted_attributes based on the test file context), the new `website_name` attribute should also be added to untrusted_attributes to prevent leaking website information to anonymous users. The test file shows tests for website_name but doesn't update the untrusted_attributes list, meaning the regression test would pass while the serializer exposes data it shouldn't.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:87 — [P2, confidence 100] `Discourse.stubs(:current_hostname).returns('forums.example.com')` exercises the parent-domain `else` branch rather than the new equal-depth sibling-subdomain branch, so the suite stays green when `www.example.com` versus `forums.example.com` incorrectly renders only the host instead of the full path.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a missing test case. Looking at the `website_name` method in the serializer, there's a specific branch for when `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and both have more than 2 parts (the sibling subdomain case like www.example.com vs forum.example.com). The test at line 87 uses 'forums.example.com' as the discourse host with 'example.com' as the website domain - these have different segment counts (3 vs 2), so it exercises the `else` branch (parent domain check), not the equal-depth sibling subdomain branch. There's no test that exercises the case where both hosts have the same number of segments > 2 (e.g., www.example.com website with forum.example.com discourse host). This is a legitimate gap in test coverage for newly added logic.
